newsitem.title: BRAZIL: TENNIS-U.S. SURVIVE SCARE TO TAKE LEAD OVER BRAZIL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-U.S. SURVIVE SCARE TO TAKE LEAD OVER BRAZIL.

text.p: The United States overcame a rowdy crowd and several sticky moments to take a 2-0 lead over underdogs Brazil in their Davis Cup World Group first round tie on Friday.
MaliVai Washington and Jim Courier both lost the opening sets of their rubbers before going on to beat opponents way below them in the world rankings.

The U.S. had to contend with fans playing trumpets and samba drums between points. The home supporters also whistled and jeered when U.S. players and staff celebrated winning points and at one stage threw pieces of cardboard on to the court.
"I'd rather not say anything about the crowd until the Davis Cup is over," commented Washington after beating Gustavo Kuerten 3-6 7-6 7-6.
Washington also had two set points against him in the second set and another two during the third.

Courier had an even more torrid time, needing three hours and 50 minutes to overcome a hugely determined Fernando Meligeni, who even made gestures to incite the crowd to make After losing the first set, Courier appeared to have taken firm control and largely silenced the crowd until a disputed point in the 10th game of the fourth set.
Brazil team captain Paulo Cleto, in what appeared to be gamesmanship as much as a genuine potest, walked on to the court to remonstrate with the umpire, sparking a chorus of jeering from the stands.

Play resumed after a two-minute interruption but Courier appeared distracted and in the very next game Meligeni broke serve to win the set. The umpire's pleas for silence were greeted with deafening boos.
Fans celebrated wildly and a hail of cardboard, handed out by sponsors for supporters to use to fan themselves, rained on to the court, prompting a warning from the umpire.
Brazil won their previous Davis Cup tie at home to Austria after Thomas Muster stormed off court in protest at crowd behaviour in Sao Paulo.

But Courier, who said beforehand that Muster had not handled the situation well, kept his cool and broke Meligeni's serve in the third game of the final set to take the match 3-6 6-4 6-1 4-6 6-4 in three hours.
"I play the drums myself and I kind of liked what they were doing," Courier said diplomatically.
